Name: Community Mod Chest
Author: Jared
Description: A collection of community-suggested content additions. Includes new apparel, weapons and armor, character-creation traits, pottery and sculpting items, comfort items, fishing gear, village content east of the River Clearing, a Clay Mound for digging clay, a Market Stall for selling trade goods, an enterable Village Inn, and an enterable Village Academy with six courses. The Village supports long-form civic growth through buildable homes, a Village Hall whose Reputation meter fills as major works are completed (also visible as a Mental attribute in your character menu), and a Boards room with seven notice boards: Village Standing, Village Projects, and one board each for the Inn Keeper, Miller, Weaver, Apothecary, and Professor. The villager boards now open directly to their notices without redundant read actions and track active errands, hints, teasers, relationship standing, and recent errand history. Includes the village timeline, resident move-ins, a daily Miller/Weaver schedule (home in their own enterable cottage overnight, standing in the village by day, with occasional wandering trips, a nightly Inn visit, and one Academy day every week — each with matching Inn/Academy card art), the Inn Keeper friendship and lost-cat storyline, the Professor's errands and milestone gifts, the Herbalism-gated Apothecary's Cabin with her own nightly Inn visit and weekly Academy day (also with matching card art), and Shadow the Cat as a separate tameable companion. The Inn Keeper and Professor react, once each, to village construction milestones (new cottages, the Village Hall, Village Reputation thresholds) and, for the Professor, to each Academy course you pass. Every winter, snow drifts block all three roads out of the Village until dug clear with a shovel. Four Town Watch guards -- Captain Reeve Sterling, Nella Thorne, Old Corrin and the night-shift Iris Vane -- take up posts around the village with three distinct jobs. Thorne and Corrin walk the Town Square by day and attack any thief or attacker they catch on village ground; Iris Vane keeps the night watch but, once your crimes brand you an enemy of the village, hunts you down anywhere on the map, day or night, and calls the rest of the Watch in rather than fighting you herself -- unlike the other three, village borders do not stop her. Talk to Captain Sterling and he gives you one formal warning the first time your standing turns Suspected -- and once you're Wanted, any guard who spots you reacts without a fight, watching you more closely, while a conversation with the Captain turns visibly colder. Any of them can be attacked, at a steep and immediate Village Crime cost; guards usually break and flee rather than die, but killing one brands you Banished for good. Only one guard fights you at a time, so a cornered criminal takes them on back to back, and a guard you nearly beat stays wounded into the next fight. Best them all and the village drops the charges entirely; each guard you put down is out of the Watch for a season before returning to their post. Losing to Thorne or Corrin gets you held, not jailed on the spot -- they pin you down and send for the Captain, but Sterling never draws on anyone. He offers to take you in peacefully and lets you walk away up to three times before he stops asking and simply takes you in unhurt, with no Bruising. When the whole Watch converges on you at once, though, he does not offer you the choice at all. Either way, the Watch has you: you wake up in the Village Jail beside the Village Hall, serving roughly a day for every 8 points of crime, with no way out of the cell until the sentence is served -- a meager daily ration of gruel and water keeps you alive without letting you thrive, backed by an emergency top-up if you ever get dangerously hungry, thirsty, or underweight, and Meditate, Sleep, and a stone-counting distraction help pass the time. Guards take turns standing warden on the jail step, in four non-overlapping shifts that cover the whole day between them, and every so often the whole Watch is off the step at once -- and during that rare gap, the cell's own bed can be shoved aside to dig at a hidden tunnel underneath. Get caught digging with the tunnel still exposed and the sentence grows and the tunnel caves back in; finish digging and crawling through clears the remaining sentence, gets you out past the walls, and marks you as an escaped convict -- worse to be caught again. All five named villagers keep a Copper Chest in their own interior -- the Miller's and Weaver's cottages, the Apothecary's Cabin, the Inn, and the Academy. Each adds salt and a little of their own trade stock to it weekly, up to a per-NPC ceiling: the Inn Keeper is the richest buyer in the village, the Miller and Weaver sit mid-tier, and the Apothecary and Professor keep thinner purses but rarer goods. You can sell valuable items to any of them, paid out of that chest's actual contents (so each can only afford what they have actually saved), or rob a chest instead if you are willing to risk being caught by its owner or the night watch. These are personal savings -- the Inn's till and the Academy's tuition account are separate and unaffected.
